candidates.summary: linkEnd/parenEnd count parentheses through a quoted title and a <...> destination, and skip an unclosed <, so a $$, \( or \[ closer after such a link is hidden: formulas master rendered turn to text, or pair with a later closer and swallow the text between
candidates.failure_scenario: `$$ [a](x "(") b $$`, `\\( [a](x "(") b \\)`, `\\[ [a](x "(") b \\]`, `\\( [a](<x(>) b \\)`, `\\( [a](<x b \\)` and `$$ [a](x 'it(s') b $$` each render one <math> at the merge base and zero at head; goldmark alone reads the link as closed (title "(", dest "x(") or as no link. Worse: `Pay $$ [a](x "(") b $$ then` + newline + `see $$ below.` pairs with the next line's $$ at head, so " then\nsee" becomes TeX; and `$$ [a](x "(") b $$` + newline + `some text` + newline + `$$` opens a display block at head (block Open now trusts findDelimClose) swallowing "some text". The same class as round 1's Warning (a destination misread hides the closer), via the title and pointy branches the space fix left; the ADR's 'It never makes a formula cross a link' and its known-limit list (only destinations that never close on their line) do not cover it. $ is unaffected: master counted parens the same way.

candidates.summary: Adding $ to the native EscapeInline set changes the result of a VM native that realms persist in state, a consensus-affecting change the PR does not call out
candidates.failure_scenario: r/gov/dao/impl/v0/prop_requests.gno:248 stores sanitize.InlineText(reason) in a treasury payment proposal's description inside a transaction. A reason holding `$` is stored as `$` by a node on the old binary and `\$` on this one, so replaying history across the upgrade, or two validators on different binaries, writes different realm state (and a different storage-byte delta/deposit). The ADR's Consequences mention only the rendered output; the native gas row (native_gas.go:179) is keyed on input length so gas itself does not move.

candidates.summary: A quoted link title holding ')' is cut by parenEnd, so a $$ inside that title still closes the expression and breaks the link, against the ADR/test claim that a link with a title stays whole
candidates.failure_scenario: `$$ [a](x "t) $$ q") c $$`: goldmark reads a; at head parenEnd stops at the ')' inside the quotes, the scan resumes in the title, and the $$ there closes: the math annotation is ` [a](x "t) ` and the link is gone. Same at the merge base (bytes.Index), so not a regression, but TestMathClosesInBracketsThatAreNoLink's 'Still whole: a link with a title' and the ADR's 'now keeps ... a link destination whole' hold only for titles without parentheses.
